summary.name: pgModeler
summary.one_liner: pgModeler is an open source, locally installed PostgreSQL schema modeling and ERD tool that supports visual design, reverse engineering, SQL generation and schema diffing.
use_cases: reverse engineer a production database into a model
generate DDL SQL scripts from a model
compare a model against a live server and generate sync statements
document database schemas with HTML data dictionaries or SVG diagrams
version control database models with Git
summary.what_it_does: pgModeler is a locally installed modeling tool for PostgreSQL that lets you visually design PostgreSQL objects such as tables, views, custom types, domains and more, and generates DDL for them. It can reverse-engineer a live PostgreSQL server into a schema model and compare a model against a server to generate ALTER, DROP and CREATE statements. Models are saved as individual, human-readable XML files that work with Git diffs. Exports include SQL scripts, PNG and SVG images, HTML data dictionaries, and direct deployment to a PostgreSQL server; a CLI supports pipeline use without the GUI. The page describes the 2.0.0-beta1 release, which adds PostgreSQL 18 temporal keys and a full Git client in the pgModeler Plus versioning plugin.
notable: Open source community edition plus commercial pgModeler Plus with reverse engineering, diff/sync, SSH tunneling and Git versioning
Models stored as one XML file per object, friendly to Git diffs and code review
Column propagation automatically creates columns and constraints when tables are linked by relationships
CLI for exporting DDL and running diffs in CI/CD pipelines
caveats: Reverse engineering, diff & sync, database management, SSH tunneling and the Git versioning plugin are Plus features
Binary packages require a download token from the key management section
Commercial editions use periodic license validation
Breaking change: default foreign key column naming pattern changed in 2.0.0-beta1
